nodes.content: Generate synchronized audio from silent video while distinguishing visually determined sound events from acoustically ambiguous alternatives.
requirements: Reduce visible-event audio onset error by 20% versus an equally sized deterministic video-to-audio baseline.
Cover 90% of reference-supported sound alternatives across samples, with visually contradicted events below 5%.

nodes.content: Train event-anchored audio diffusion with frame-level onset supervision and uncertainty-conditioned sampling gated against visually contradicted events.
How can sampling preserve frame-accurate visible-event onsets while exploring plausible sounds without generating visually contradicted events?
Event-anchored, uncertainty-sampled, visually gated diffusion yields ≥20% lower onset MAE than deterministic audio, ≥90% alternative recall, and <5% visual contradictions.
Annotate multi-reference clips; train uncertainty-conditioned, event-anchored diffusion with visual gating; compare onset MAE, alternative recall, contradiction rate against matched baseline.
Annotate 1,200 SilentSound-MR clips with visible-event onset frames, reference-supported sound alternatives, and visually contradicted event labels.
SilentSound-MR v1: 1,200 clips with frame-indexed event onsets, reference-supported sound alternatives, and visually contradicted event labels.
Audit SilentSound-MR v1 labels; train matched-size diffusion and deterministic models; measure held-out onset MAE, alternative recall, and contradiction rate.
On SilentSound-MR v1, onset MAE improved 24% versus the deterministic baseline, but alternative recall was 78% and contradictions 8%.
Onset-locked event stems with stratified sound sampling and visual-consistency reranking should reach ≥90% alternative recall and <5% contradictions.
On held-out SilentSound-MR v1, ablate onset-locked stems, stratified sampling, and visual reranking; measure onset MAE, alternative recall, and contradictions.
On SilentSound-MR v1, revised sampling achieved 92% alternative recall, 3.8% contradictions, and 23% lower onset MAE than the deterministic baseline.
Adopt revised sampling: 92% recall and 3.8% contradictions correct the initial 78%/8% failures while preserving 23% onset-MAE improvement.
Evaluate leave-one-event-category-out SilentSound-MR v1 splits, comparing revised event-anchored diffusion against matched deterministic baseline on onset MAE, alternative recall, contradiction rate.
Across leave-one-category-out splits, event-anchored diffusion lowered onset MAE 21% versus baseline, with 90% alternative recall and 4.6% contradictions.
Can visual gating reject implausible impacts without suppressing reference-supported off-screen sounds in occluded SilentSound-MR clips?
Use optical-contact tracks for onset-constrained audio retrieval, sampling multiple sound libraries while rejecting candidates contradicted by visible motion.
Extract optical-contact tracks, retrieve diverse library sounds, align candidate transients, filter visual contradictions, and benchmark against deterministic baseline on SilentSound-MR.
Benchmark optical-contact retrieval against event-anchored diffusion and the deterministic baseline on SilentSound-MR v1, measuring onset MAE, alternative recall, and contradictions.
On SilentSound-MR v1, optical-contact retrieval cut onset MAE 22% versus baseline, but achieved 74% alternative recall and 6.2% contradictions.
Are limited sound-library coverage and motion-only filtering responsible for retrieval’s 74% alternative recall and 6.2% visual contradictions?
Library expansion should raise alternative recall from 74% to ≥90%; semantic visual filtering should lower contradictions from 6.2% to <5%.
Ablate library expansion and semantic filtering on SilentSound-MR v1, measuring alternative recall, contradictions, and off-screen retention in occluded clips.
On SilentSound-MR v1, expanded-library retrieval with semantic filtering achieved 91% alternative recall, 4.2% contradictions, and 88% off-screen retention.
Reconsider optical-contact retrieval after its failed initial benchmark: library expansion and semantic filtering now achieve 91% recall and 4.2% contradictions.
Run leave-one-category-out tests of revived retrieval against diffusion and deterministic baseline, including occluded events; report onset MAE and coverage errors.
SilentSound-MR benchmark report: leave-one-category-out and occlusion results comparing revived retrieval, diffusion, and deterministic baseline across onset MAE, recall, and contradictions.
Recompute the benchmark report’s category and occlusion metrics from archived predictions, auditing split leakage and baseline parameter parity.
Leakage-free category splits: revived retrieval reduced onset MAE 21% versus matched baseline, with 90% alternative recall and 4.7% contradictions.
Select diffusion over revived retrieval: both meet targets, but diffusion has fewer contradictions (4.6% versus 4.7%).
Use a causal event graph to lock visible onsets, branch over ambiguous sound sources, and synthesize visually consistent audio.
Can causal event edges reject incompatible sound-source combinations without pruning supported alternatives or shifting locked impact onsets?
On SilentSound-MR v1, compare causal graph synthesis, edgeless branching, and deterministic baseline using alternative recall, contradiction rate, onset MAE.
On SilentSound-MR v1, causal graph synthesis achieved 89% alternative recall, 3.5% contradictions, and 22% lower onset MAE versus baseline.
Softening low-confidence causal edges should raise alternative recall from 89% to ≥90% while retaining <5% contradictions and ≥20% onset-MAE reduction.
Calibrate causal-edge confidence on SilentSound-MR v1 training clips; soften uncertain exclusions, then benchmark held-out recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
Use benchmark report category failures to prioritize soft-edge calibration on training clips; test held-out recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
SoftEdgeGraph v1: calibrated causal-edge weights, category-specific exclusion thresholds, and held-out recall, contradiction, and onset-MAE evaluation logs.
Re-run SoftEdgeGraph v1 held-out evaluation against hard-edge graph and deterministic baseline; audit thresholds, alternative recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
Held-out SoftEdgeGraph v1 achieved 91% alternative recall, 4.1% contradictions, and 21% lower onset MAE than deterministic baseline.
Prioritize SoftEdgeGraph for matched-split comparison: it reports 91% recall and 4.1% contradictions versus retrieval’s 90% and 4.7%.
Occlusion-aware causal edges should halve incompatible source pairings versus edgeless branching while maintaining ≥90% alternative recall and ≥20% onset-MAE reduction.
Benchmark occlusion-aware SoftEdgeGraph, edgeless branching, revised diffusion, and deterministic baseline on occluded clips: incompatible pairings, recall, contradictions, onset MAE.
Occluded clips: graph recall fell to 86%; diffusion achieved 91% recall, 3.9% contradictions, and 22% lower onset MAE versus baseline.
Train a frame-aligned audio-token transformer with event-boundary heads and diverse nucleus decoding, rejecting visually incompatible token sequences.
Boundary-supervised audio tokens with diverse decoding should achieve ≥20% lower onset MAE, ≥90% alternative recall, and <5% contradictions.
Using SoftEdgeGraph v1 exclusion thresholds, benchmark the boundary-supervised token transformer against the deterministic baseline: onset MAE, alternative recall, contradictions.
On SilentSound-MR v1, the token transformer reduced onset MAE 20% versus baseline, with 90% alternative recall and 4.9% contradictions.
Keep diffusion primary; prefer SoftEdgeGraph over token transformer: recall 91% versus 90%, contradictions 4.1% versus 4.9%.
Validate diffusion against SoftEdgeGraph on independent occluded clips; release only if onset MAE, alternative recall, and contradiction targets hold.
Evaluate frozen diffusion and SoftEdgeGraph on 300 independent occluded clips against a matched deterministic baseline, scoring onset MAE, recall, contradictions.
SoftEdgeGraph v2 replaces v1’s held-out-only logs with 300-clip independent occlusion onset-MAE, recall, and contradiction comparisons against frozen diffusion.
Audit SoftEdgeGraph v2’s 300 occluded clips; rerun causal-graph and token-transformer predictions against diffusion on onset MAE, recall, contradictions.
On 300 independent occluded clips, token transformer achieved 90% alternative recall, 4.8% contradictions, and 21% lower onset MAE versus baseline.
Retain diffusion as primary; reopen the SoftEdgeGraph-versus-transformer choice for occlusions, since independent transformer results meet all targets.
Do event-boundary heads prevent onset drift during overlapping occluded impacts while nucleus decoding preserves supported sound alternatives?
Identify overlapping impacts in SoftEdgeGraph v2’s 300 clips; ablate boundary heads and nucleus decoding; measure onset drift and alternative recall.
Ablations exposed per-event macro-averages across 300 clips: the full transformer improved onset MAE 17% versus baseline; alternative recall was 87%.
